channel.description: Latest articles from CT News Junkie (ctnewsjunkie.com)

item.title: Poll: Lamont Holds ‘Comfortable Lead’ For Dem Nod
item.description: Gov. Ned Lamont holds a comfortable lead in his bid for the Democratic nomination for governor, according to a Nutmeg State Poll released this week.

item.title: CT House Speaker Warns Republicans Of ‘Reactions’ To Filibustering Bills With Broad Bipartisan Support — ‘Don’t Do It’
item.description: Some of S.B. 298’s sections included in its 121 pages include a section on municipal pensions that the Connecticut Conference of Municipalities called a costly mandate, and some funding earmarks that House and Senate Republicans have said should be reexamined.

item.title: CT Reaches $5M Settlement Deal Between 544-Unit Apartment Complex And Its Tenants
item.description: The $5.1 million financial relief plan is one of two such agreements being negotiated between the state and JRK Property Holdings to resolve the investigation into the management and conditions at the 544-unit complex.

item.title: Stanley Black & Decker To Close New Britain Manufacturing Plant, About 300 Jobs Impacted
item.description: The Stanley Works was founded in New Britain in 1843 and later merged with Maryland-based Black & Decker in 2010.

item.title: CT Motorists Can Honor Puerto Rican ‘Borinqueneers’ With New License Plate
item.description: Nicknamed the Borinqueneers, the 65th Infantry Regiment of the United States Army earned a reputation for bravery, discipline, and devotion to duty despite facing segregation, discrimination and language barriers.

item.title: ACLU To Host Webinar On License Plate Readers, Flock Cameras
item.description: The American Civil Liberties Union of Connecticut is hosting a webinar next week on automatic license plate readers, including Flock cameras.

item.title: Family Weighs Wrongful Death Suit After Hartford 211 Call Ends In Fatal Police Shooting
item.description: Hartford police Lt. Aaron Boisvert said the officers involved were placed on administrative leave while the Inspector General investigates whether the use of deadly force was justified under state law, though no other comment was provided.

item.title: Should CT Tax Tips And Overtime Work? House Republicans Say No As Committee Hears Testimony
item.description: The bill was scheduled for a public hearing and potential action in the Finance, Revenue and Bonding Committee Friday afternoon.

item.title: Federal Research Cuts Hit UConn
item.description: While UConn has not been individually targeted by Trump or engaged in high-profile battles with the president like other universities such as Harvard, Columbia, and Brown, it has been impacted by the administration’s unprecedented research grant cuts and changes to federal funding totaling $95 million.

item.title: CT Officials React To Iran Strikes
item.description: Iran later retaliated with ballistic missile attacks against targets in Israel, Bahrain, UAE, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia, according to reports.
